stem: Which of the following relation is not correct?
solution:
$H = U + PV$ (by definition)

$\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta(PV)$; at constant pressure $\Delta H = \Delta U + P\Delta V$

Hence $\Delta H = \Delta U - P\Delta V$ is not correct.
notes: options C and D are printed identically in the source

stem:
Among the following the correct statements are:

I. $\text{LiH}$, $\text{BeH}_2$ and $\text{MgH}_2$ are saline hydrides with significant covalent character

II. Saline hydrides are volatile

III. Electron-precise hydrides are Lewis bases

IV. The formula for chromium hydride is CrH

The correct option is:
solution:
I is correct: $\text{LiH}$, $\text{BeH}_2$, $\text{MgH}_2$ have significant covalent character. II is wrong: saline hydrides are non-volatile crystalline solids. III is wrong: electron-precise hydrides (e.g. $\text{CH}_4$) are neither Lewis acids nor bases; electron-rich hydrides are Lewis bases. IV is correct: chromium forms the metallic hydride CrH.

Hence I and IV only.

stem:
In which of the following reactions does $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ act as an oxidising agent (either in acidic, alkaline or neutral medium)?

(i) $2\text{Fe}^{2+} + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow$

(ii) $2\text{MnO}_4^- + 6\text{H}^+ + 5\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow$

(iii) $\text{I}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 + 2\text{OH}^- \rightarrow$

(iv) $\text{Mn}^{2+} + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow$
solution:
Completing the reactions:

(i) $\text{Fe}^{2+} + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \longrightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

(ii) $\text{MnO}_4^- + \text{H}^+ + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \longrightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + \text{O}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

(iii) $\text{I}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 + \text{OH}^- \longrightarrow \text{I}^- + \text{O}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

(iv) $\text{Mn}^{2+} + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \longrightarrow \text{Mn}^{4+} + \text{OH}^-$

In reactions (i) and (iv), $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ acts as oxidising agent and itself gets reduced.

stem: The charge on colloidal particles is due to
options: adsorption of ions from the solution
solution: Colloidal particles acquire charge by preferential adsorption of ions (common to the particle) from the dispersion medium.

stem: Which of the following is correct order of ligand field strength?
solution: The increasing order of field strength of ligands (according to spectrochemical series): $\text{S}^{2-} < \text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} < \text{NH}_3 < en < \text{CO}$

stem: In the Victor-Meyer's test, the colour given by $1^\circ$, $2^\circ$ and $3^\circ$ alcohols are respectively:
solution:
(i) $1^\circ$: $\text{RCH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{HI}} \text{RCH}_2\text{I} \xrightarrow{\text{AgNO}_2} \text{RCH}_2\text{NO}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{HNO}_2}$ nitrolic acid $\xrightarrow{\text{KOH}}$ blood red colour

(ii) $2^\circ$: $\text{R}_2\text{CHOH} \xrightarrow{\text{HI}} \text{R}_2\text{CHI} \xrightarrow{\text{AgNO}_2} \text{R}_2\text{CHNO}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{HNO}_2}$ pseudonitrol $\xrightarrow{\text{KOH}}$ blue colour

(iii) $3^\circ$: $\text{R}_3\text{COH} \xrightarrow{\text{HI}} \text{R}_3\text{CI} \xrightarrow{\text{AgNO}_2} \text{R}_3\text{CNO}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{HNO}_2}$ no reaction $\xrightarrow{\text{KOH}}$ colourless

stem: Which one of the following is a water soluble vitamin, that is not excreted easily?
solution:
Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) are stored in liver and adipose tissue; water-soluble vitamins (B-complex and C) are usually not stored and excess is excreted in urine.

However, Vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$ (cobalamin) is an exception: the body can store it in the liver for several years, so it is not excreted as easily as $\text{B}_1$, $\text{B}_2$ or $\text{B}_6$.

The correct answer is Vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$.

stem: Calculate the activation energy of a reaction, whose rate constant doubles on raising the temperature from $300$ K to $600$ K.
Which one of the following compounds is having maximum 'lone pair-lone pair' electron repulsions?
solution: $\text{XeF}_2$ has three lone pairs and two bond pairs. The three lone pairs are arranged in the equatorial positions because of which they face maximum repulsion from each other.

stem: The correct statement among the following is;
options: Ferrocene has two cyclohexadiene rings coordinated to iron atom.
Ferrocene has two cyclopentadienyl anion rings bonded to iron (II) ion.
Perxenate ion is tetrahedral is shape.
solution:
Ferrocene is $\text{Fe}(\eta^5\text{-C}_5\text{H}_5)_2$.

Perxenate ion is $[\text{XeO}_6]^{4-}$ which is octahedral.
